1. No, I would not perform rifampicin drug-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen. This is because the Xpert MTB/RIF test has already detected rifampicin resistance, so further testing would be redundant and unnecessary.

2. To determine the dose of each drug for this patient, I would use the patient's weight and the standard dosing guidelines for pulmonary tuberculosis treatment. The typical dosing for a patient with normal renal function and no other significant comorbidities is as follows: Isoniazid (INH) 5 mg/kg/day, Rifampicin (RIF) 10 mg/kg/day, Pyrazinamide (PZA) 20-25 mg/kg/day, and Ethambutol (EMB) 15-20 mg/kg/day. For a 16-year-old patient, the doses would be approximately: INH 300 mg/day, RIF 300 mg/day, PZA 400-500 mg/day, and EMB 300-400 mg/day.
